newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norsk Hydro mulls Venezuela aluminium buy.
newsitem.headline: Norsk Hydro mulls Venezuela aluminium buy.

text.p: Norwegian industrial group Norsk Hydro ASA may invest in Venezuela's aluminium industry, which is heading for privatisation by the end of the year, the business daily Dagens Naeringsliv said on Wednesday.

Hydro is one of 12 companies registered to qualify to bid for a share in the Venezuelan state industry, which includes aluminium producers Venalum and Alcasa, bauxite and alumina producer Bauxilum and anode plant Carbonarca.
The ventures are all based in Ciudad Guayana in the northeast of the country and will be disposed of together, the newspaper said.
Hydro Aluminium has been seeking to expand its aluminium activities outside Norway for some time as part of a strategy to serve markets outside Europe.
If Hydro successfully bids for a Venezuelan stake, it could almost double its total aluminium production capacity and gain large resources of alumina and bauxite, Dagens Naeringsliv said.
Venezuela has two aluminium smelters with an output of around 640,000 tonnes per year. Hydro's capacity currently stands at 675,000 tonnes per year.

Dagens Naeringsliv said that most other large aluminium producers had also put in bids for a slice of the Venezuelan activities, including Alcoa, Alcan, Reynolds, Kaiser, Alumax, Glencore, Billiton, Oremet, Marubeni and Mitsubishi.
Since the late 1980s Hydro has been supplying technology and production line equipment to Venalum, but the group wanted to find out about other sides of the operations.
"We have qualified ourselves for the bidding round to get information (of the privatisation)," Thomas Knutzen, chief spokesman for Hydro Aluminium, was quoted as saying.
"We don't know, for example, if there is an environmental bomb linked to bauxite production or other such things which could have heavy consequences for us."
Hydro registered itself as a single investor but has not ruled out taking part in a consortium, Dagens Naeringsliv said.
